# INTRX — The Interaction Library

> A curated, copy-paste library of the web interactions used by award-winning
> design agencies. 399 native patterns are implemented, including the full 52-entry DRAMS collection.
> Each pattern ships three things: a live demo, a single-file HTML+CSS+JS
> snippet, and an LLM prompt that specifies the interaction precisely enough
> to rebuild it in any framework.

Site: https://intrx.vercel.app
Registry: https://intrx.vercel.app/registry/index.json
License: MIT; photographs under the Unsplash License with per-component attribution. DRAMS by 1042 Studio (@mrblackstudio and @karimeshrimp).

## Buttons & Micro

### Border Beam (`btn-border-beam`)

Build an original self-contained Border Beam control matching the v4 INTRX tile: one 160 by 40px charcoal Deploy button, 12px corners, a 1px white border at 11% opacity, a white 16px lightning icon and 13.5px medium Inter. Center it on a transparent 260 by 100 design plane. The shell supplies the stage and dock; render no outer panel, header, measurement labels or replay/reset buttons. Use the supplied local SVG icon, 121 by 1px perimeter highlight and 76 by 32px glow without resizing their intrinsic dimensions. A regular rounded-rectangle CSS motion path moves the light around the button over 2000ms linear. Pause/resume retains its current position, and a shell replay action returns to the top-center peak frame. Press scales to .97 over 80ms ease-out; release takes 250ms ease-pop. Expose toggle and replay through ctx.onAction and announce button activation through a live status and ctx.emit. Under reduced motion freeze the top-center highlight, keep keyboard focus and activation feedback, and use a 150ms opacity press response. Support native Enter/Space, runtime suspension, declared geometry and portable local assets.

Center it on a transparent 260 by 100 design plane. Render no specimen card, telemetry labels or internal toolbar. A masked neutral gradient with a 26px soft white band and background-size 400% sweeps from background-position 100% to 0% over 2000ms linear, repeating while visible. Expose toggle and replay with ctx.onAction; pause retains the exact position and replay restarts the pass. Use a native button with visible focus, Enter/Space activation, a live status and ctx.emit for the invitation action. Press to .97 in 80ms ease-out and release in 250ms ease-pop. Keep running/sweeps/entries/inside/activations telemetry off the visible surface. Reduced motion renders the centered still sheen and uses 150ms opacity feedback. The shell owns the stage, lifecycle, fit and dock controls.

### Jelly Press (`btn-jelly-press`)

Build an original tactile Jelly Press matching the v4 tile: a single soft #f1f1f1 button measuring 140 by 36px, 12px corners, a restrained shadow, dark #111 text and 13px medium Inter reading Press and hold. Center it on a transparent 260 by 100 design plane. Hold to compress to scale(1.10,.82) over 80ms ease-out around a 50% 65% origin and reduce the shadow. Keep the squash until the matching primary pointer or Space/Enter is released; do not run a timed one-shot while the user is holding. On release read the actual current transform and use a time-based spring with stiffness 380, damping 32 and mass 1, integrated in 1/120s steps, to return to rest with a small rebound. Preserve position if a fresh press interrupts the spring. Capture the pointer so an outside release is handled; cancellation, lost capture, blur and replay must release or clear safely. Ignore duplicate/secondary presses and key repeats while preserving native button activation. Expose run through ctx.onAction for a simulated 250ms hold, plus replay for immediate cancellation. Use wrapped timers and frames, remove window listeners on disposal, keep visible focus and a hidden live status, and emit native activations. Reduced motion keeps the shape static and provides a 150ms opacity change while held. No demo-owned panels or reset buttons; every class starts with d-jelly-demo.

## Navigation & Menus

### Fullscreen Menu (`menu-fullscreen-overlay`)

## Scroll

### Lenis Smooth Scroll (`lenis-smooth-scroll`)

Implement Lenis smooth scrolling on my website.

Requirements:
- Use the "lenis" npm package (or CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1.1.14/dist/lenis.min.js).
- Initialize with lerp around 0.09-0.1 for a smooth but responsive feel.
- For a component preview use a fixed 320px-tall inner scroll container. Keep the styled root outside the Lenis wrapper, whose class name must not contain the substring "lenis" because Lenis 1.x rewrites that substring. Give the inner viewport keyboard focus and overscroll containment. Use editorial editorial serif headings and a clear scroll cue at native size.
- Drive it with a requestAnimationFrame loop (lenis.raf(time)).
- If GSAP ScrollTrigger is present, sync them: lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update) and drive Lenis from gsap.ticker instead of a raw rAF loop.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: skip Lenis entirely when the user has it enabled.
- Destroy the Lenis instance and cancel its animation frame when unmounting or resetting.
- Anchors (#links) should still work: intercept clicks and call lenis.scrollTo(target).

Final typography: Use Newsreader at normal weight for the main editorial text. Use Inter for actions and readable interface copy; retain regular Inter counters, coordinates and technical annotations. Keep material borders subdued and gradients broad with continuous, gentle falloff.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders. Any deliberate Newsreader editorial text in the source remains editorial, not UI.

### Staggered Scroll Reveal (`scroll-reveal-stagger`)

Build a staggered scroll-reveal system in vanilla JS (no libraries).

Requirements:
- Elements marked with a data-reveal attribute start at opacity 0 and translateY(40px).
- When they enter the viewport (IntersectionObserver, threshold ~0.25), they animate to opacity 1 / translateY(0) using a cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) ease over ~0.7s.
- Siblings inside the same container stagger by ~80ms each, via a CSS custom property for transition-delay.
- The animation should reverse when scrolled out, so it replays on re-entry.
- Use only CSS transitions driven by a class toggle — no per-frame JS.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion by showing elements immediately.

Use three equal flexible columns in the native narrow preview, with 8px gaps, 24px outer padding, compact 11px Inter labels, and grayscale card surfaces.

### Parallax Depth Layers (`parallax-layers`)

Build a vanilla-JS parallax section.

Requirements:
- A tall scroll region with a position:sticky scene inside it.
- Multiple absolutely-positioned layers, each with a data-speed attribute (0.2 = far background, 1.0 = foreground).
- On scroll, translateY each layer by scrollY * (1 - speed) * 0.5 so layers separate with depth.
- Use a passive scroll listener and transform only (no top/margin changes) so it stays on the compositor.
- Add will-change: transform to the layers.
- Before interaction, show a subtle animated scroll cue; stop it permanently on first pointer or keyboard interaction.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion by disabling the effect.

Final typography: Use Inter for the main display or interface text. Use Inter for actions and readable interface copy; retain regular Inter counters, coordinates and technical annotations. Keep material borders subdued and gradients broad with continuous, gentle falloff.

### Sticky Stacking Cards (`sticky-stack`)

Build a sticky stacking-cards scroll section, vanilla JS + CSS.

Requirements:
- A list of full-width cards, each position: sticky with the same top offset, so each new card pins over the previous.

- Passive scroll listener; transforms only.
- Before interaction, show a subtle animated scroll cue; stop it permanently on first pointer or keyboard interaction.

### Scroll Velocity Skew (`velocity-skew`)

- Map velocity to a skewY target, clamped to about ±12deg.

### Proximity Type (`proximity-type`)

Build a proximity-reactive headline (mac-dock effect for letters), vanilla JS.

Requirements:
- Split the headline into per-character spans (display: inline-block).
- Track the cursor globally; in a rAF loop compute each letter's distance from the cursor via getBoundingClientRect centers.
- Influence t = max(0, 1 - dist / 140) passed through smoothstep (t*t*(3-2t)).
- Apply transform: translateY(-22px * ease) scale(1 + 0.35 * ease), and tint letters above ~0.35 influence with an accent color.
- Park the cursor at -9999 on mouseleave so letters settle back.
- Optional upgrade: with a variable font, also map ease to font-variation-settings wght.
- Disable on touch devices and under prefers-reduced-motion.

Use a medium-weight sans-serif headline, native 24px padding, and container-relative sizing. Tint influenced letters #fa7319 while the remaining letters stay light gray.

### Text Falling Letters (`text-falling-letters`)

Build a self-contained phrase “FALL INTO PLACE” as thirteen independent glyph bodies. Keep one focusable field with button semantics and an accessible label; split only the visual phrase into aria-hidden spans while preserving real-width spaces.

Use semi-implicit Euler physics in one requestAnimationFrame loop: vy += 1900*dt, then position += velocity*dt. Measure per-letter floor and horizontal bounds from real DOM rectangles. On floor collision clamp y, reverse vy with restitution 0.48, damp vx and angular velocity with friction 0.78, and sleep a body once vertical bounce is small and horizontal/angular speeds are below thresholds. Side walls reverse vx with coefficient 0.64. Stop the loop when every body sleeps.

### Magnetic Button (`magnetic-button`)

Build magnetic buttons with GSAP.

Requirements:
- On mousemove over the button, compute the cursor offset from the button center.
- Translate the button toward the cursor at ~0.4 of the offset, and the inner label at ~0.7 (parallax between shell and label).

- On mouseleave, both animate back to 0,0 with elastic.out(1, 0.35) over ~0.9s for a springy snap-back.
- The label must be pointer-events: none so it never steals hover.
- Disable on touch devices.
- If GSAP is unavailable, describe a vanilla fallback using lerp in requestAnimationFrame.

Use regular Inter for all labels. Bold changes the sample to weight500; Italic, Case, Left and Right visibly edit it; Reset clears the format. Every control is a real semantic button with keyboard activation and pressed state. Root keyboard shortcuts B/I/C/arrows/R are available when the bank itself has focus. No fake telemetry, repeated debug footers or microcounters. Honor reduced motion and teardown.

## Sound & Haptics

### UI Sound Kit (`ui-sound-kit`)

Use a native 300 by 320 composition. Turn four tiny technical sound pads into a readable sound palette, with synthesis specs hidden. Use locally bundled Inter at weights 400–550 for UI and every numerical readout, with tabular numerals and normal tracking. Monospace is reserved for actual code or ASCII. Create/resume AudioContext exclusively inside a click gesture and route voices through a master gain. Synthesize: short square hover tick, sine confirm plus delayed octave, downward saw warning, and two-note square toggle. Pitch varies by pad index. Add mute/unmute, visual envelope pulse, log reset, and enabled/muted/events/last/hits/context/source telemetry. Never autoplay audio.

### Typing Mechanical (`typing-mechanical`)

Use a native 300 by 320 composition. Replace dark faux typewriter paper with a readable note surface and quiet key response. Use locally bundled Inter at weights 400–550 for UI and every numerical readout, with tabular numerals and normal tracking. Monospace is reserved for actual code or ASCII. Preserve pointer, keyboard, deterministic fixtures, reset behavior and lifecycle contracts. Build a gesture-gated mechanical typing field. On each printable key, Enter, or Backspace, derive velocity as clamp(1−interKeyDelta/420,.08,1). Synthesize a 75ms falling triangle body plus 45ms band-passed noise whose filter and gain rise with velocity. Show the last six keys and physical travel, plus a velocity meter. Include enable, mute, reset, and enabled/muted/strokes/lastKey/velocity/pitch/context/source telemetry. Never autoplay audio.

### Theremin Pad (`theremin-pad`)

Use a native 300 by 320 composition. Make pitch and volume manipulation visible in a soft two-dimensional pad with readable direction labels. Use locally bundled Inter at weights 400–550 for UI and every numerical readout, with tabular numerals and normal tracking. Monospace is reserved for actual code or ASCII. Preserve pointer, keyboard, deterministic fixtures, reset behavior and lifecycle contracts. Build a press-only WebAudio theremin. During pointer contact map normalized x logarithmically from 220 to 880Hz and inverted y from .015 to 1 amplitude, smoothing oscillator frequency and gain with setTargetAtTime. Stop with a 40ms release on pointerup/cancel. Record up to 120 normalized trace points on canvas. Add sine/triangle/saw switching, A4 center preset, clear/reset, and pressed/frequency/gain/wave/points/gestures/context/source telemetry. Audio must never start before pointerdown.

### Drum Grid Sequencer (`drum-grid-sequencer`)

### Scroll Pitch Drone (`scroll-pitch-drone`)

Measure an internal scroll viewport as abs(Δy/Δt), scale/clamp velocity to 0–2.5, and map it to base frequency 180–260Hz and cutoff 220–2700Hz. Click emits a radial impulse; each dot returns to its original position. Use a 320px-high near-black stage, a disciplined grayscale palette with #fa7319 as the only accent, and crisp 1px linework. Move the pointer · click to send a wave. Support Pointer Events, proportional local coordinates, arrow-key navigation and Enter activation. Cap canvas DPR at 2 and delta time at 32ms; resize using ResizeObserver. Stop rendering when offscreen, and cancel animation frames and disconnect observers on unmount. Respect live prefers-reduced-motion changes with a representative static state and direct input updates. Keep HTML, CSS, and JavaScript standalone with no network dependencies.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders.
